name: Astryx
works_with: React 19 or later, with Next.js, Vite, Tailwind or plain CSS; any coding agent through its CLI
short: Meta's open source React design system: 150+ accessible components, themes, dark mode and a CLI your coding agent can read.
what: Astryx grew inside Meta over eight years and now ships as an open source design system. You get 150+ accessible components, brand theming, dark mode, page templates and a CLI. You import pre-built CSS and typed React components, with no build plugin. The CLI gives you and your agent the same component docs.
who: React developers who want a full component library and are happy on React 19. It suits teams that let an agent write UI, because the CLI tells the agent which components exist. Skip it if you are not on React.

steps.title: Tell your agent about it
steps.text: `init` writes the Astryx component index into your `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, so your agent finds components and design tokens.

steps.title: Import the CSS
steps.text: For Next.js, put these three lines in `src/app/globals.css`. The order matters.

steps.title: Wrap your app in the theme
steps.text: Wrap your app in `<Theme theme={neutralTheme}>` from `@astryxdesign/core/theme`. The core package README has the full Next.js, Tailwind, Vite and CDN versions.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `npx @astryxdesign/cli component Button` for the full docs on one component, or `astryx template dashboard` to get the source for a full dashboard page.

watch: Always use the scoped name `@astryxdesign/cli`. Until it is a dependency, the plain `astryx` name points to an unrelated npm package.
The chart packages are only on the `@canary` tag, with no stable release yet.
